1. Overview and base URL

This guide covers integrating with the Payments REST API to create and manage payments, refunds, and payment methods, and to receive asynchronous events through webhooks.

Base URLs

EnvironmentBase URLPurpose
Sandboxhttps://sandbox.api.example-pay.com/v1Testing with simulated card networks and test keys. No real money moves.
Productionhttps://api.example-pay.com/v1Live transactions. Use only after passing certification.

All requests must use HTTPS. Requests over plain HTTP are rejected with a 400 response. Request and response bodies use application/json; charset=utf-8.

Versioning and idempotency

The version is part of the path (/v1). Non-breaking changes such as new optional fields or new endpoints are released within v1. Build clients to ignore unknown fields.

All POST requests that create resources accept an Idempotency-Key header. Send a unique value (for example, a UUID v4) per logical operation. If a request is retried with the same key and the same body, the original response is returned. Keys are retained for 24 hours.

Amounts. All amounts are integers in the smallest currency unit (for example, cents for USD: 2500 means $25.00). Never send floating-point amounts. Currency codes follow ISO 4217 in lowercase or uppercase.

2. Authentication

The API uses API keys sent as Bearer tokens in the Authorization header. Each project has separate sandbox and production keys.

Key types

PrefixEnvironmentUse
sk_test_SandboxServer-side calls in testing
sk_live_ProductionServer-side calls with live money. Never expose in client code.
pk_test_ / pk_live_EitherPublishable key for client-side tokenization only. Cannot read or create charges.

Making an authenticated request

Authorization: Bearer sk_test_51Nx...redacted
Content-Type: application/json

Key management guidance

  • Store secret keys in a secrets manager or environment variables. Do not commit them to source control.
  • Rotate keys from the dashboard. Old keys remain valid for 24 hours after rotation so you can deploy safely.
  • Restrict each key to the minimum scope needed (for example, payments:write, refunds:write, read_only).
  • Use separate keys per service so you can revoke one without affecting others.
Security. If a secret key is exposed, revoke it immediately in the dashboard. Requests using a revoked key return 401 unauthorized.

3. Endpoints

All paths are relative to the base URL. Resource IDs use prefixes: pay_ (payment), ref_ (refund), pm_ (payment method), whk_ (webhook endpoint), evt_ (event).

MethodPathDescriptionIdempotent
POST/paymentsCreate a payment and attempt to capture funds.Via Idempotency-Key
GET/paymentsList payments. Supports limit, starting_after, status, and created_after filters.Yes
GET/payments/{id}Retrieve a single payment.Yes
POST/payments/{id}/captureCapture a previously authorized payment. Optional amount for partial capture.Via Idempotency-Key
POST/payments/{id}/cancelVoid an authorized payment that has not been captured.Via Idempotency-Key
POST/refundsRefund all or part of a captured payment.Via Idempotency-Key
GET/refunds/{id}Retrieve a refund.Yes
POST/payment_methodsStore a tokenized payment method for later use.Via Idempotency-Key
GET/payment_methods/{id}Retrieve a stored payment method (masked details only).Yes
DELETE/payment_methods/{id}Detach a stored payment method from its customer.Yes
POST/webhook_endpointsRegister a URL to receive event notifications.Via Idempotency-Key
GET/events/{id}Retrieve an event object. Events are kept for 30 days.Yes

Pagination

List endpoints return up to limit items (default 10, maximum 100). The response includes has_more. To fetch the next page, pass the id of the last item as starting_after.

4. Request and response examples (JSON)

4.1 Create a payment

Request — POST /v1/payments

{
  "amount": 2500,
  "currency": "usd",
  "payment_method": "pm_1NxQ7a2eZvKYlo2C",
  "capture": true,
  "description": "Order #10482",
  "customer": "cus_9sLk3Xe1",
  "metadata": {
    "order_id": "10482"
  }
}

Response — 201 Created

{
  "id": "pay_3MtwBwLkdIwHu7ix28a3tqPa",
  "object": "payment",
  "amount": 2500,
  "amount_captured": 2500,
  "amount_refunded": 0,
  "currency": "usd",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "payment_method": "pm_1NxQ7a2eZvKYlo2C",
  "customer": "cus_9sLk3Xe1",
  "description": "Order #10482",
  "metadata": {
    "order_id": "10482"
  },
  "created": 1763892000,
  "livemode": false
}

4.2 Create a payment that requires action

Some payments (for example, 3-D Secure) return requires_action. Redirect the customer using next_action.redirect_url, then confirm the result by retrieving the payment or waiting for a webhook.

{
  "id": "pay_4QvRk8LmnXy2Hb71",
  "object": "payment",
  "amount": 15000,
  "amount_captured": 0,
  "currency": "eur",
  "status": "requires_action",
  "next_action": {
    "type": "redirect_to_url",
    "redirect_url": "https://hooks.example-pay.com/3ds/pay_4QvRk8LmnXy2Hb71"
  },
  "created": 1763892410,
  "livemode": false
}

4.3 Partial refund

Request — POST /v1/refunds

{
  "payment": "pay_3MtwBwLkdIwHu7ix28a3tqPa",
  "amount": 1000,
  "reason": "requested_by_customer"
}

Response — 201 Created

{
  "id": "ref_1PqZ0vLkdIwHu7ix",
  "object": "refund",
  "payment": "pay_3MtwBwLkdIwHu7ix28a3tqPa",
  "amount": 1000,
  "currency": "usd",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "reason": "requested_by_customer",
  "created": 1763892700,
  "livemode": false
}

4.4 List payments

Request — GET /v1/payments?limit=2&status=succeeded

{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    { "id": "pay_3MtwBwLkdIwHu7ix28a3tqPa", "object": "payment", "amount": 2500, "currency": "usd", "status": "succeeded", "created": 1763892000 },
    { "id": "pay_7HsJd2KpQo9Wn4Le", "object": "payment", "amount": 4200, "currency": "usd", "status": "succeeded", "created": 1763890113 }
  ],
  "has_more": true
}

4.5 Error response

{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "amount_too_small",
    "message": "The amount must be at least 50 cents for USD.",
    "param": "amount",
    "request_id": "req_Xk29sLmQ81ZpRt"
  }
}

5. curl examples

Set your key once in the shell. Examples use the sandbox base URL.

export PAY_API_KEY="sk_test_51Nx...redacted"
export PAY_BASE="https://sandbox.api.example-pay.com/v1"

5.1 Create a payment

curl -X POST "$PAY_BASE/payments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2a4e-9b3d-4c7a-8e21-0d5f9a7b3c11" \
  -d '{
    "amount": 2500,
    "currency": "usd",
    "payment_method": "pm_1NxQ7a2eZvKYlo2C",
    "capture": true,
    "metadata": { "order_id": "10482" }
  }'

5.2 Retrieve a payment

curl "$PAY_BASE/payments/pay_3MtwBwLkdIwHu7ix28a3tqPa" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAY_API_KEY"

5.3 List succeeded payments, 20 per page

curl -G "$PAY_BASE/payments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAY_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "status=succeeded" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=20"

5.4 Authorize now, capture later

# Step 1: authorize only
curl -X POST "$PAY_BASE/payments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 0b7e9d12-4f6a-4e8b-9c35-7a1d2e4f6b88" \
  -d '{ "amount": 8000, "currency": "usd", "payment_method": "pm_1NxQ7a2eZvKYlo2C", "capture": false }'

# Step 2: capture 6500 of the 8000 authorized
curl -X POST "$PAY_BASE/payments/pay_5RtUv9WxYz1Ab2Cd/capture" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 3d4e5f60-1a2b-4c3d-8e9f-a0b1c2d3e4f5" \
  -d '{ "amount": 6500 }'

5.5 Partial refund

curl -X POST "$PAY_BASE/refunds" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-9c2d-1e0f9a8b7c6d" \
  -d '{ "payment": "pay_3MtwBwLkdIwHu7ix28a3tqPa", "amount": 1000, "reason": "requested_by_customer" }'

5.6 Register a webhook endpoint

curl -X POST "$PAY_BASE/webhook_endpoints" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PAY_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: 2c3d4e5f-6a7b-4c8d-9e0f-1a2b3c4d5e6f" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://www.example.com/webhooks/payments",
    "events": ["payment.succeeded", "payment.failed", "refund.succeeded"]
  }'

Note: The curl examples use -G with --data-urlencode for query parameters so that values are encoded correctly.

6. Error codes

Errors use standard HTTP status codes. The body always contains an error object with type, code, message, and request_id. Include request_id when contacting support.

HTTP statusError codeTypeMeaning and what to do
400invalid_requestinvalid_request_errorMalformed JSON or missing required field. Fix the request; do not retry unchanged.
400amount_too_smallinvalid_request_errorAmount is below the currency minimum (for example, 50 cents for USD).
400currency_not_supportedinvalid_request_errorThe currency is not enabled for your account.
401unauthorizedauthentication_errorMissing, malformed, or revoked API key.
402card_declinedcard_errorThe issuer declined the payment. Check decline_code for details (for example, insufficient_funds). Ask the customer for another method.
403forbiddenauthentication_errorThe key lacks the scope required for this operation.
404resource_missinginvalid_request_errorNo resource with that ID exists in this environment. Check you are using the right sandbox or production key.
409idempotency_conflictinvalid_request_errorThe Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request body.
409invalid_stateinvalid_request_errorThe operation is not valid for the payment's current status (for example, capturing a payment that is already captured).
422payment_method_unusablecard_errorThe stored payment method is expired or has been detached.
429rate_limitedrate_limit_errorToo many requests. Wait for the time in the Retry-After header, then retry with exponential backoff.
500internal_errorapi_errorUnexpected server error. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key.
502 / 503 / 504service_unavailableapi_errorTemporary upstream or maintenance issue. Retry with backoff and the same Idempotency-Key.
Retry guidance. Retry only on 429 and 5xx responses, and on network timeouts. Always reuse the original Idempotency-Key so a retry cannot create a duplicate charge. Do not retry other 4xx responses without changing the request.

7. Webhooks

Webhooks push events to your server when something changes, such as a payment succeeding or a refund failing. Use them to update your system asynchronously instead of polling.

Event types

EventTriggered when
payment.succeededA payment is captured successfully.
payment.failedA payment attempt is declined or errors out.
payment.requires_actionThe customer must complete an additional step, such as 3-D Secure.
payment.canceledAn authorized payment is voided.
refund.succeededA refund is settled.
refund.failedA refund is rejected by the network.
payment_method.detachedA stored payment method is removed from a customer.

Event payload

{
  "id": "evt_1NxW3pLkdIwHu7ix",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "payment.succeeded",
  "created": 1763892005,
  "livemode": false,
  "api_version": "v1",
  "data": {
    "object": {
      "id": "pay_3MtwBwLkdIwHu7ix28a3tqPa",
      "object": "payment",
      "amount": 2500,
      "currency": "usd",
      "status": "succeeded"
    }
  }
}

Signature verification

Each delivery includes a Payments-Signature header in the form t=<unix_timestamp>,v1=<hex_signature>. The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of the string <timestamp>.<raw_request_body>, keyed with your endpoint's signing secret (whsec_...).

  1. Read the raw request body before any JSON parsing.
  2. Compute the expected signature and compare it with v1 using a constant-time comparison.
  3. Reject requests whose timestamp is more than 5 minutes from your server time.

Delivery and retries

  • Respond with any 2xx status within 10 seconds. Process heavy work asynchronously.
  • Any other response, or a timeout, counts as a failure and triggers retries with exponential backoff for up to 72 hours.
  • Deliveries are at least once. Deduplicate using the event id.
  • Events may arrive out of order. Use the created timestamp or re-fetch the object from the API before acting on it.
Endpoints that repeatedly fail are disabled after 50 consecutive failed deliveries. Re-enable them from the dashboard after fixing the receiver.

8. Rate limits

Rate limits are applied per API key and per environment. Limits are shared across all servers using the same key.

ScopeLimitWindow
Read requests (GET)100 requestsper second
Write requests (POST, DELETE)25 requestsper second
Concurrent in-flight requests20per key

Rate limit headers

Every response includes the following headers:

HeaderDescription
RateLimit-LimitThe request limit for the current window.
RateLimit-RemainingRequests left in the current window.
RateLimit-ResetSeconds until the window resets.
Retry-AfterIncluded on 429 responses only. Seconds to wait before retrying.

Handling 429 responses

  • Wait for Retry-After seconds before retrying.
  • If the header is absent, use exponential backoff starting at 1 second, with random jitter.
  • Reuse the original Idempotency-Key for write requests.
  • Prefer webhooks over polling. If you must poll, keep it under 10 requests per second per key.
Higher limits. Contact support to request higher limits for high-volume integrations. Include your account ID and expected peak requests per second.

Document version 1.0. Limits, retention periods, and event types are subject to change; check the changelog in the developer dashboard for updates.
